history.titleZh: US mulling ban on key Chinese networking tech in data center component crackdown — White House wants to impose restrictions in 2026, China says it will respond if necessary
history.descriptionZh:
美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）正在制定一项新规，计划禁止进口中国制造的光模块（optical transceivers）。这类组件在数据中心中承担着关键角色——将电脉冲信号转换为光信号进行传输，再将光信号转回电信号，是高速数据传输的核心器件。据路透社援引消息人士的话称，FCC希望该规定能在今年年底前正式生效。

这一禁令背后是日益严峻的数据中心供应链安全担忧。AI政策专家、咨询公司Beacon Global Strategies的Divyansh Kaushik表示：“光模块确实构成风险。随着数据中心建设规模不断扩大，你需要确保数据中心供应链从头到尾都是安全的。”美方担心这些组件可能被用于窃取数据、植入恶意软件或干扰美国数据中心正常运行。

光模块之所以成为数据中心不可或缺的部件，是因为相比传统铜缆布线，光纤通信功耗更低、传输速度也快得多。目前美国本土也有光模块制造商，如Lumentum、Coherent和Apple Optoelectronics（苹果光电），但路透社指出，这些企业在规模和产能上都无法与行业龙头Innolight（中际旭创）相抗衡——后者已占据全球市场27%的份额。

这并非FCC近几个月来首次实施针对特定行业的禁令。美国自2019年起就已禁止华为产品进入本国市场，而近期又陆续出台了一系列主要影响中国企业或与中国有关联企业的禁令，包括：2025年12月生效的外国制造无人机禁令、去年4月生效的外国制造路由器禁令，以及上个月刚刚宣布的针对重量超过4.4磅且具备200kbps连接能力的高级机器人设备的禁令。

第一项禁令主要针对大疆（DJI）；4月颁布的路由器禁令则重创了TP-Link，尽管该公司已于2024年与其中国母公司分离。需要注意的是，7月公布的机器人禁令虽然看似与普通消费者无关，但实际影响范围相当广——它涵盖了扫地机器人，而美国市场上的主流品牌如iRobot、Roborock（石头科技）、Ecovacs（科沃斯）、Dreame（追觅）和小米等，其背后实体均为中国企业。

尽管美方声称这些禁令适用于所有企业，但也允许有条件豁免。例如，Netgear和亚马逊已成功为其外国制造型号争取到2027年10月前的豁免权。TP-Link在4月也申请了额外批准，但至今未获批复。

有分析认为，FCC希望在中国的光模块组件在美国AI数据中心中普及之前就将其拦截在外。这正是华为案例留下的教训——华为产品在被禁时已深度嵌入美国系统，导致后续移除和替换所有华为组件的工作耗时数年、成本高昂。

中国驻华盛顿大使馆回应称，中方敦促美国“倾听两国商界的客观理性声音”，“停止污蔑中国企业和以制裁相威胁”，并警告将对任何损害中国利益的行为采取“必要措施”予以回应。北京此前已有过类似反制行动——去年，为回应华盛顿的EDA软件禁令，中国禁止了对美稀土出口，最终迫使白宫收回了相关决定。

history.title: NVIDIA Joins NSF State and Regional AI Hubs Program to Expand AI Research and Education Across the US
history.description: NVIDIA is participating in the U.S. National Science Foundation’s (NSF) State and Regional Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Hubs program, an effort launching today to expand access to the advanced computing, data, software and expertise needed for AI-enabled research and education. Consistent with the aims of the Genesis Mission, the program will support state and multistate groups […]
history.content: NVIDIA is participating in the U.S. National Science Foundation’s (NSF) State and Regional Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Hubs program, an effort launching today to expand access to the advanced computing, data, software and expertise needed for AI-enabled research and education. Consistent with the aims of the Genesis Mission, the program will support state and multistate groups of colleges and universities working together to strengthen America’s AI ecosystem. In partnership with private industry, philanthropic organizations and state and local governments, the program will expand the AI infrastructure, software, educational resources and technical support needed by faculty, students and researchers across the country. These regional hubs will help institutions share AI computing resources, accelerate scientific discovery and innovation, and prepare students to participate in the AI economy. Expanding Access to AI Infrastructure The State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs program will bring shared resources closer to the institutions and communities they serve. State or regional consortia can pool expertise, focus on specific local priorities, achieve economies of scale and create pathways for institutions that might otherwise remain outside the frontier of AI-enabled research and education. Flexible approaches — including on-premises infrastructure, cloud computing or a combination — will allow consortia to design resources around their regional needs and economic priorities. The hubs will resemble the public-private partnership between NVIDIA, NVIDIA cofounder Chris Malachowsky and the University of Florida (UF) in 2020 to turn UF into the country’s first true AI university and provide AI compute access to all Florida public universities. That initiative now serves as a national model. Since launching its university-wide initiative in 2020, UF has grown to more than 300 AI-focused faculty and embedded AI education and research across all 16 colleges. And since 2017, UF faculty and units have received more than $511 million in AI research awards. NVIDIA has also expanded academic compute access in other ways, including as a leading contributor to the NSF-led National Artificial Intelligence Research Resource (NAIRR) pilot program on which today’s announcement is built. Through NAIRR, NVIDIA partnered with university research teams across the country to turn computing resources into usable scientific capacity — giving researchers the infrastructure, tools and expertise needed to move from idea to experiment to discovery. The resources also facilitated meaningful educational opportunities that gave students critical real-world skills for the AI economy. Preparing the AI Workforce AI infrastructure alone is not enough. A successful national AI strategy must include efforts to build a workforce that can use advanced computing, data resources and AI tools in real scientific and industry settings. That means pairing infrastructure with clear learning pathways. Universities, community colleges and regional partners can build degree programs, short-form certificates and stackable credentials that help learners move from foundational AI literacy into applied skills. Those pathways will help students, faculty, working adults and technical professionals use AI, including open source models and technologies, in fields like physical AI and automation, healthcare, energy, agriculture, manufacturing, quantum computing and cybersecurity. NVIDIA can support this work by providing training resources, educator enablement, applied learning content, technical guidance, partner platforms and access to tools that help institutions move from awareness to hands-on capability. As NVIDIA’s education and training offerings evolve, the goal remains the same: help institutions build repeatable, openly available programs that prepare learners to use AI systems, accelerated computing and data workflows responsibly and effectively. This is how regional hubs become more than infrastructure projects. Students gain practical experience. Faculty expand their ability to teach and apply AI across disciplines. Working professionals can earn new skills without leaving the workforce. And institutions can connect training to local employer needs, research priorities and the economic opportunities that matter most to their communities. Connecting Research, Workforce and Regional Growth For policymakers and leaders, the hubs offer an opportunity to connect regional research and educational infrastructure with regional priorities and broader workforce and economic-development strategies. Institutions can cultivate talent for local needs, support research connected to regional industries and build stronger relationships among universities, community colleges, employers and government. These connections will help translate AI leadership into scientific progress, new businesses and high-quality jobs. No single organization can build this capacity alone. Sustained collaboration among government, higher education, philanthropic organizations and private industry is essential to ensure that advanced AI resources are broadly available and effectively used. Private-sector contributions can complement public investment with technology, implementation expertise and workforce development programs. Public institutions, in turn, can help direct those capabilities toward scientific, educational and economic priorities that advance regional needs and national interest. Learn more about the NSF State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs program and how NVIDIA is helping expand access to AI research and education.

美国国家科学基金会（NSF）于今日正式启动“州级与区域人工智能基础设施中心”计划，旨在扩大美国各地高校和科研机构获取AI所需先进计算、数据、软件及专业知识的渠道。英伟达作为该计划的核心参与方，将与美国政府、高等教育界、慈善组织和私营企业共同构建覆盖全国的AI研究与教育基础设施网络。

这一计划与“创世纪使命”（Genesis Mission）的目标高度一致，将支持州级或多州联合的大学联盟，通过共享算力资源、协同创新来强化美国的AI生态系统。计划的核心理念是让AI资源更贴近服务对象——州级或区域联盟可以汇集各自专长，聚焦本地优先事项，实现规模经济，并为那些原本可能被排除在AI前沿之外的高校开辟参与路径。在基础设施部署方式上，计划提供灵活选择，包括本地部署、云端计算或两者结合，使各联盟能够根据区域需求和经济重点量身定制资源配置方案。

值得注意的是，这项计划的重要蓝本是英伟达与其联合创始人Chris Malachowsky及佛罗里达大学（UF）在2020年建立的公私合作模式。该合作将佛罗里达大学打造为全美第一所真正的AI大学，并将AI算力开放给佛罗里达州所有公立大学使用。这一举措现已发展为国家级示范项目：自2020年启动全校AI计划以来，佛罗里达大学已拥有超过300名专注AI研究的教师，AI教育和研究已嵌入全部16个学院；自2017年起，该校教师和院系累计获得超过5.11亿美元的AI研究经费。

英伟达还通过其他渠道拓展学术算力获取途径，包括作为NSF主导的“国家人工智能研究资源”（NAIRR）试点项目的主要贡献者——今天宣布的计划正是在NAIRR的基础上构建的。通过NAIRR，英伟达与全美高校研究团队合作，将算力转化为可用的科研能力，为研究人员提供了从想法到实验再到发现所需的基础设施、工具和专业知识，同时这些资源也创造了宝贵的教育机会，让学生获得了AI经济所需的实操技能。

在英伟达看来，仅提供AI基础设施远远不够。一个国家级的成功AI战略必须包含劳动力培养体系，使人们能够在真实的科学研究和产业环境中驾驭先进计算、数据资源和AI工具。这意味着基础设施必须与清晰的学习路径相结合：大学、社区学院和区域合作伙伴可以构建学位项目、短期证书和可叠加的微认证体系，帮助学习者从AI基础素养逐步进阶到应用技能。这些路径将服务于学生、教师、在职成人和技术专业人员，涵盖物理AI与自动化、医疗健康、能源、农业、制造业、量子计算和网络安全等多个领域。

为此，英伟达将提供培训资源、教育者赋能、应用学习内容、技术指导、合作伙伴平台以及工具访问等全方位支持，帮助各机构从“认知AI”过渡到“动手实操”的能力阶段。随着英伟达教育和培训产品不断演进，其核心目标始终不变：帮助院校建立可重复、可公开获取的项目，培养学习者负责任且有效地使用AI系统、加速计算和数据工作流的能力。

这一模式将使区域中心超越单纯的基础设施项目：学生获得实践经验，教师拓展跨学科教学与研究AI的能力，在职专业人员无需离开工作岗位即可获得新技能，院校则能将培训与本地雇主需求、研究重点和社区最关心的经济机遇对接。对于政策制定者和领导者而言，这些中心提供了一个将区域科研和教育基础设施与区域优先事项、劳动力培养及经济发展战略相连接的契机——各机构可以为本地区培养急需人才，支持与区域产业相关的研究，并加强大学、社区学院、雇主和政府之间的合作关系，将AI领导力转化为科学进步、新创企业和高质量就业机会。

英伟达强调，没有任何单一组织能够独自完成这项能力建设。政府、高等教育、慈善组织和私营企业之间的持续协作至关重要——私营部门的贡献可以用技术、实施经验和劳动力发展项目补充公共投资，而公共机构则可以将这些能力引导到推动区域需求和国家利益的科研、教育及经济优先方向上。

history.title: NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Super, the Frontier Open Model for Robotaxis and Autonomous Vehicles, Now Available for Commercial Use

history.content: For robotaxis and other autonomous vehicles (AVs), the hardest problems aren’t the everyday scenarios. They’re the rare, complex situations that are difficult to anticipate and train for. Handling these long‑tail events takes more than just object detection and motion prediction. AVs must understand the situation, reason about cause and effect, choose the right action and turn that decision into a safe, comfortable path — all in real time and in a way developers can inspect, validate and trust. NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Super, available now for commercial use, is part of the Alpamayo family, the most-adopted open reasoning models for autonomous driving on Hugging Face, supporting a wide range of AV-relevant capabilities within a single foundation model. Built on NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Super Reasoner and post‑trained with reinforcement learning, the model advances the AV ecosystem on two fronts: open commercial licensing and leading multitask capabilities for autonomous driving. Alpamayo 2 Super is part of NVIDIA’s growing collection of open models, datasets and tools for autonomous driving, expanding access, strengthening competition, giving developers greater control and supporting safer, more transparent AV deployment. Open Licensing for Production AVs Alpamayo 2 Super is available on Hugging Face under OpenMDW‑1.1, the Linux Foundation’s permissive license for open AI model distributions. The license covers fine‑tuning, derivative models and commercial redistribution, allowing AV developers, automakers, truckmakers and suppliers to adapt Alpamayo to their own data, driving policies and deployment strategies. This openness lets AV researchers and companies keep control of their own data and infrastructure, as well as own the value they create through specialized models and accumulated know‑how. Such control is essential for workflows involving proprietary fleets and safety. Earlier Alpamayo releases were initially introduced for R&D. The OpenMDW license is now being applied across the entire Alpamayo model family so developers can deploy any of the models commercially without requiring additional permissions. This creates a direct path from adaptation to deployment. Open weights make that path economically viable. Teams can build on advanced reasoning without re‑training every foundation capability from scratch or paying frontier‑model costs for every task, matching the right model to the right job at the right cost. Alpamayo 2 Super enables frontier-scale reasoning in cloud-based development workflows, where developers can generate high-quality reasoning traces, synthetic training data and teacher outputs for model distillation. Within the Alpamayo model family, Alpamayo 2 Super delivers the highest reasoning and driving performance for multimodal autonomous driving development, while Alpamayo 1.5 and Alpamayo 1 provide more cost-efficient options for cloud-based development and model distillation. The resulting distilled models can then be optimized for efficient, real-time inference in production vehicles. Together, the Alpamayo model family provides a cloud-to-car workflow that combines frontier-scale reasoning with scalable deployment across commercial AV fleets. For AV programs, that means frontier‑scale reasoning in the cloud and efficient, specialized models in the vehicle — a more sustainable way to scale safe autonomy into commercial fleets. Benchmark-Leading Reasoning at Frontier Scale Alpamayo 2 Super ranks first on LingoQA, an autonomous driving reasoning benchmark, among nearly 40 models evaluated. In NVIDIA testing using the Lingo‑Judge metric, it outperformed Qwen2.5‑VL 72B by 17.0 points, Gemini 2.5 Pro by 15.1 points and GPT‑4o by 23.2 points, demonstrating state‑of‑the‑art reasoning for driving‑centric scenarios. Alpamayo 2 Super also ranks first across all autonomous driving benchmarks evaluated by NVIDIA, underscoring its leading performance across a broad range of AV capabilities. Alpamayo 2 Super offers 3x the scale of the 10‑billion‑parameter NVIDIA Alpamayo 1.5 and Alpamayo 1 models. The added capacity helps the model better generalize reasoning from sparse examples — a critical capability for the rare, multi‑agent interactions where conventional systems often struggle. The model reasons over full‑surround camera coverage, fusing views from the vehicle’s front, sides and rear. This 360‑degree context enables richer understanding of lane changes, merges, unprotected turns and complex intersections, where risks commonly arise. A Multitask Foundation Model for Robotaxis and Autonomous Driving For each driving situation, Alpamayo 2 Super can produce five tightly coupled outputs: A trajectory describing the vehicle’s planned path. A chain‑of‑causation (CoC) trace that explains the reasoning behind the decision. A meta‑action (e.g., yield, lane changes, stops) that captures the model’s intent. Reasoning auto-labels that generate CoC annotations for training and validation data. Visual question answering responses with 2D visual grounding that link the model’s answers to specific regions in camera images. Together, these outputs offer insight into the model’s decision-making process. Developers can tie what the model observed to the action it selected, making decisions easier to understand, critique and validate. CoC traces integrate with NVIDIA Halos safety‑validation workflows and support AI safety aligned with ISO/PAS 8800 requirements, providing a stronger foundation for AV safety engineering. Alpamayo 2 Super can also be deployed as an autolabeler to generate CoC labels and perform visual question answering with 2D grounding on proprietary fleet data. By linking its reasoning to specific regions in camera images, the model can transform raw driving clips into richer training data, compressing annotation cycles from months to days. Beyond planning and auto-labeling, Alpamayo 2 Super supports scene understanding, model critiquing and knowledge distillation. These multitask capabilities enable developers to use a single foundation model across more of the development stack, simplifying tooling and accelerating iteration. An Open Ecosystem for Reasoning‑Based AVs Alpamayo 2 Super is part of a broader family of open models, frameworks and datasets for AV development. Other tools in the family include: NVIDIA AlpaSim, which provides closed‑loop simulation. NVIDIA AlpaGym, which enables high‑throughput reinforcement learning. NVIDIA Physical AI Open Datasets, which supply data for training and testing. Open training recipes and an autolabeling pipeline to accelerate model development, training and validation. Alpamayo has already surpassed 500,000 downloads on Hugging Face, reinforcing its position as the most-adopted open reasoning model family for autonomous driving on the platform. Download NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Super on Hugging Face to explore the model, evaluate its reasoning capabilities and start building the next generation of robotaxis and autonomous vehicles.

history.titleZh: NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Super：面向Robotaxi与自动驾驶的前沿开放模型，现已开放商用
history.descriptionZh:
在自动驾驶领域，真正棘手的挑战并非日常驾驶场景，而是那些难以预判和训练的罕见复杂情况。应对这些"长尾事件"，仅靠目标检测和运动预测远远不够——自动驾驶车辆必须理解场景、推理因果关系、选择正确行动，并将决策转化为安全舒适的行驶轨迹，整个过程需实时完成，且结果必须可检查、可验证、值得信赖。NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Super正是为此而生，现已面向商业应用开放。作为Hugging Face上自动驾驶领域采用最广泛的开源推理模型家族Alpamayo的最新成员，它在一个基础模型中整合了多种自动驾驶关键能力。

Alpamayo 2 Super基于NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Super Reasoner构建，并通过强化学习进行后训练，在两大方向推动了自动驾驶生态系统的进步：开放商业许可以及领先的多任务自动驾驶能力。该模型是NVIDIA不断扩充的自动驾驶开源模型、数据集和工具集合的一部分，旨在扩大技术可及性、增强行业竞争、赋予开发者更多控制权，并支持更安全、更透明的自动驾驶部署。

**面向量产自动驾驶的开放许可**

Alpamayo 2 Super已在Hugging Face上以OpenMDW-1.1许可证发布——这是Linux基金会为开放AI模型分发提供的宽松许可。该许可覆盖微调、衍生模型和商业再分发，允许自动驾驶开发者、汽车制造商、卡车制造商和供应商根据自有数据、驾驶策略和部署方案定制Alpamayo。这种开放性使自动驾驶研究团队和企业能够保留对数据和基础设施的控制权，同时保有通过专用模型和积累的技术诀窍所创造的价值。对于涉及专有车队和安全性的工作流而言，这种控制至关重要。

此前Alpamayo系列模型的早期版本主要面向研发用途，如今OpenMDW许可已适用于整个Alpamayo模型家族，开发者无需额外授权即可将任一模型投入商业部署。这一转变打通了从适配到落地的直接路径，而开放权重使该路径在经济上切实可行——团队可以在不从头重新训练全部基础能力、也无需为每项任务支付前沿模型费用的情况下，基于先进推理能力进行开发，以合理的成本将合适的模型匹配到合适的任务。

Alpamayo 2 Super支持云端开发工作流中的前沿规模推理，开发者可借此生成高质量的推理轨迹、合成训练数据以及用于模型蒸馏的教师模型输出。在Alpamayo家族内部，Alpamayo 2 Super为多模态自动驾驶开发提供了最强的推理和驾驶性能，而Alpamayo 1.5和Alpamayo 1则提供了更具成本效益的云端开发和模型蒸馏选项。蒸馏后的模型可进一步优化，以实现在量产车辆中的高效实时推理。整个Alpamayo模型家族由此构成了从云端到汽车的完整工作流，将前沿规模的推理能力与商用自动驾驶车队的大规模部署有机结合——即在云端进行前沿规模的推理，在车端部署高效专用模型，以更可持续的方式将安全自动驾驶扩展至商用车队。

**基准测试领先的前沿规模推理**

Alpamayo 2 Super在自动驾驶推理基准LingoQA上，于近40个参评模型中排名第一。在NVIDIA使用Lingo-Judge指标的测试中，它分别超越Qwen2.5-VL 72B达17.0分、Gemini 2.5 Pro达15.1分、GPT-4o达23.2分，展现出面向驾驶场景的最先进推理能力。在NVIDIA评估的全部自动驾驶基准中，Alpamayo 2 Super同样排名第一，凸显了其在广泛自动驾驶能力维度的领先表现。

Alpamayo 2 Super的规模是100亿参数的NVIDIA Alpamayo 1.5和Alpamayo 1模型的3倍。增加的模型容量使其能够更好地从稀疏样本中泛化推理——这正是应对传统系统往往力不从心的罕见多智能体交互场景的关键能力。该模型可对全周环绕摄像头覆盖进行推理，融合车辆前、侧、后方的多视角信息。这种360度上下文使其能够更深入地理解变道、汇入、无保护转弯和复杂路口等高风险场景。

**面向Robotaxi与自动驾驶的多任务基础模型**

针对每种驾驶情境，Alpamayo 2 Super可生成五种紧密耦合的输出：描述车辆规划路径的轨迹；解释决策背后推理的因果链（CoC）追踪；捕捉模型意图的元动作（如让行、变道、停车）；为训练和验证数据生成CoC标注的推理自动标注；以及具备2D视觉定位功能的视觉问答响应，可将模型的答案关联到摄像头图像中的特定区域。

这些输出共同揭示了模型的决策过程。开发者可以将模型观察到的内容与其选择的行动关联起来，使决策更易于理解、评判和验证。CoC追踪与NVIDIA Halos安全验证工作流集成，并支持符合ISO/PAS 8800要求的AI安全实践，为自动驾驶安全工程奠定了更坚实的基础。

Alpamayo 2 Super还可作为自动标注器部署，在专有车队数据上生成CoC标签并执行带2D视觉定位的视觉问答。通过将推理与摄像头图像的特定区域关联，该模型能将原始驾驶片段转化为更丰富的训练数据，将标注周期从数月压缩至数天。

除规划和自动标注外，Alpamayo 2 Super还支持场景理解、模型评判和知识蒸馏。这些多任务能力使开发者能够在更多开发环节中使用单一基础模型，从而简化工具链并加速迭代。

**基于推理的自动驾驶开放生态系统**

Alpamayo 2 Super是更广泛的自动驾驶开源模型、框架和数据集家族的一部分。其他配套工具包括：提供闭环仿真的NVIDIA AlpaSim、支持高吞吐强化学习的NVIDIA AlpaGym、为训练和测试提供数据的NVIDIA Physical AI Open Datasets，以及加速模型开发、训练和验证的开源训练配方和自动标注流水线。

Alpamayo在Hugging Face上的下载量已突破50万次，巩固了其作为该平台最受采纳的自动驾驶开源推理模型家族的地位。开发者现可下载NVIDIA Alpamayo 2 Super，探索其推理能力，并着手构建下一代Robotaxi和自动驾驶车辆。

history.title: Chinese chipmaking tool roadmaps examined — Beijing's nascent lithography tools target DUV production at five machines a year, and an EUV prototype with no chips
history.description: Ultimately, three markers will indicate whether China’s domestic DUV program is a legitimate rival or yet more state-sanctioned hot air.
history.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter China has started low-volume production of domestically developed immersion DUV lithography machines, with around five systems planned for this year and roughly 20 in 2027, according to a report from July 27, which wiped roughly $44 billion off ASML's market value.The manufacturer was named as Shanghai Aishengna Electronic Technology Group by Reuters the following day, a state-owned company established in August 2023 with 7 billion yuan (around $1 billion) in registered capital that absorbed engineering teams from Huawei-affiliated startup Yuliangsheng and state scanner maker SMEE. The first units are due at SMIC, Hua Hong, and CXMT this year for production-line validation rather than volume output, but the machines are far from matching ASML's models and still require further testing.Five machines represent about 3.8% of the roughly 130 immersion systems ASML deploys in a typical year (a class of lithography machines that put a super thin layer of liquid over the wafer during processing), with the European giant holding an estimated 98.7% of the total immersion market. The Chinese tool reportedly prints 28nm-class features in a single exposure and reaches 7nm, and theoretically 5nm, through multipatterning, the same route SMIC already runs on its installed ASML fleet. Neither company has confirmed the report, no machine has been shown publicly, and no throughput or overlay figures have been disclosed, against the 330 wafers per hour and 2.5nm overlay of ASML's current flagship immersion tools.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: SMIC’s scannerSMIC has been running a domestic immersion scanner, developed under the codename Mount Everest, since September last year, when the Financial Times reported that China's largest foundry had begun testing the Yuliangsheng tool with production-line integration targeted from 2027 after qualification.FT compared the machine against ASML's Twinscan NXT:1950i, a system that entered the market in 2008, which puts the design roughly a decade and a half behind the tools ASML sells today. Yuliangsheng, founded in Shanghai in 2022 with 1 billion yuan (around $149 million) in registered capital, is understood to have delivered three lithography machines to fabs for testing by late last year, but this hasn’t been officially confirmed. You may like China begins mass production of homegrown immersion chipmaking machines in major breakthrough, report claims Shanghai Aishengna named as the maker of China's first domestic immersion DUV chipmaking tools SMIC founder and AMEC CEO urge Chinese fabs to test domestic chipmaking tools on active production lines Many of the critical components needed for the machines are still imported from Japan, and delays at those local suppliers are what have capped 2026 output at around five units. The 2027 target of 20 machines is therefore an ambitious target that assumes a domestic component base that hasn't been established yet, and the imported parts remain within reach of any future export-control round.18% litho localizationSMEE's most advanced shipping product remains the SSA600 series, a 90nm-class dry ArF scanner that was in mass production as of May last year. The 28nm-capable SSA/800 immersion tool the company announced in 2023 has never been deployed, and a state-media claim of its successful development was deleted shortly after publication. In December last year, SMEE won a roughly RMB 110 million ($16 million) single-source government contract for a KrF scanner specified at 110nm resolution and 15nm overlay, a useful indicator of where its production-grade capability is at the moment.Domestic equipment took 35% of Chinese fab purchases in 2025, beating Beijing's 30% target and up from about 10% three years earlier, according to figures from China's semiconductor industry association. Etch and thin-film deposition passed 40% localization, and metrology reached 25%, while lithography managed just 18%, most of it in trailing-edge and packaging tools. From the end of 2025, new fab capacity additions are required to source at least half their equipment domestically, a mandate that guarantees the new scanners a customer base, whatever their specs turn out to be.Etch, deposition, and everything else (Image credit: ASML)Naura Technology became the world's fifth-largest chip equipment maker by 2025 sales, trailing only ASML, Applied Materials, Lam Research, and Tokyo Electron, and moving ahead of KLA. The company booked RMB 27.14 billion ($4 billion USD) in revenue in the first three quarters of 2025 against RMB 6.05 billion ($589 million USD) for all of 2020, holds an order backlog stretching into 2027, and has started developing lithography tools for the first time. AMEC grew revenue and net profit by more than 30% in 2025, while cleaning specialist ACM Research posted $901.3 million for fiscal 2025 and guided to as much as $1.18 billion for 2026.SiCarrier, the Shenzhen firm widely linked to Huawei, debuted around 30 tools at SEMICON China in March 2025, spanning etch, deposition, metrology, and test, and was reportedly valued at RMB 65 billion ($9.63 billion USD) by September 2025 with more than RMB 10 billion ($1.48 billion USD) in orders. The U.S. added it to the Entity List in December 2024. What to read next Chinese startup claims photonic chip production without DUV lithography, says nanoimprint process cuts costs by 90% ASML's planned Low-NA EUV machine price hikes reportedly anger TSMC Trailing-edge foundry roadmaps for GlobalFoundries, UMC, and SMIC The sector's own leadership is less triumphant than the numbers suggest. In March, SMIC co-founder Wang Yangyuan and the heads of YMTC, Naura, and EDA firm Empyrean jointly described China's tool industry as "small, fragmented, and weak" and called for national consolidation, with Big Fund III's $47.5 billion being redirected toward lithography and EDA. The Aishengna venture, which merged the Yuliangsheng and SMEE teams into one state-owned vehicle, looks like the first product of that pressure to consolidate. China spent a record $49.5 billion on wafer fab equipment in 2024, per SEMI, and remains the world's largest buyer through 2027, even after a pullback in 2025.EUV lithography A Reuters investigation in December 2025, dubbed China’s “Manhattan Project,” described an operational prototype EUV light-source machine in a high-security Shenzhen lab, completed in early 2025, that generates EUV photons but hasn't yet exposed a wafer. More than 3,000 researchers are said to work across the program, with Huawei playing the coordinating role and SMEE handling system integration.Two teams are chasing the light source: one led by Lin Nan, a Beihang University professor who worked at ASML from 2015 to 2021, has a solid-state laser-produced-plasma design running at 3.42% conversion efficiency against the roughly 5.5% commercial viability required, while Zhao Yongpeng's laser-assisted discharge plasma group at Harbin Institute of Technology has reached around 100W of EUV output against the roughly 600W that ASML's production sources deliver.Beijing's target is chip output from the machine by 2028, with Reuters' sources calling 2030 more realistic. A separate strand of reporting described a reverse-engineered prototype built around an intercepted Cymer light source that has likewise produced nothing. Earlier claims of a Huawei EUV trial production in 2025 and mass production in 2026, which circulated via Chinese media in March 2025, were never confirmed by any primary source. Tsinghua University's accelerator-based SSMB concept, which would need a synchrotron of a staggering 100 to 150 meters in circumference, remains an academic project.Export controlsThe MATCH Act, introduced in the House and Senate in early April, would ban not only sales of immersion DUV tools to SMIC, Huawei, Hua Hong, CXMT, and YMTC but also the servicing of machines already installed, and would give the Netherlands and Japan 150 days to align.At this stage, it remains a bill, not a law, but servicing restrictions would strike directly at the installed ASML base that produces every advanced chip China currently makes, including SMIC's N+3 node in Huawei's Kirin 9030. Chinese fabs have been preparing for exactly that scenario by using third-party engineers and gray-market parts to Frankenstein older ASML machines.ASML's China exposure is already shrinking on schedule, with the country representing 20% of system sales compared to 41% in 2024 and 33% last year, even as the company raised full-year guidance to €43 to €45 billion in July. Likewise, Applied Materials expects to lose $600 to $710 million in China revenue this fiscal year.Ultimately, three markers will indicate whether China’s domestic DUV program is a legitimate rival or yet more state-sanctioned hot air. The main one would be validated production wafers from an Aishengna tool at SMIC, Hua Hong, or CXMT with published throughput and yield, followed by delivery of anything close to the 20 machines planned for 2027, and a first exposed wafer from the Shenzhen EUV prototype before the 2028 target set by Beijing.

中国自主研发的浸没式DUV光刻机已启动小批量生产。据7月27日报道，今年计划生产约5台设备，2027年将增至约20台，这一消息直接导致ASML市值蒸发约440亿美元。次日，路透社确认制造商为上海埃斯纳电子科技集团——这家成立于2023年8月的国有企业，注册资本70亿元人民币（约10亿美元），吸纳了华为关联初创公司宇量升光和国有光刻机厂商上海微电子装备（SMEE）的工程团队。首批设备预计今年交付中芯国际、华虹和长鑫存储进行产线验证，而非量产输出，但该设备与ASML的机型相比仍有明显差距，需要进一步测试。

从规模上看，5台设备仅占ASML年交付约130台浸没式系统（该类光刻机在加工过程中会在晶圆表面覆盖一层超薄液体）的3.8%，而这家欧洲巨头据估计掌控着浸没式光刻市场98.7%的份额。据报道，这款国产设备单次曝光可印制28纳米级特征，通过多重曝光工艺可达7纳米，理论上甚至能触及5纳米——这正是中芯国际在其现有ASML设备上已采用的路线。目前两家公司均未证实该消息，没有任何机器公开展示，也未披露产能或套刻精度参数。作为对比，ASML当前旗舰浸没式设备的产能为每小时330片晶圆，套刻精度为2.5纳米。

中芯国际自去年9月就已开始运行一款代号为"珠穆朗玛峰"的国产浸没式光刻机。当时英国《金融时报》报道，这家中国最大晶圆代工厂已开始测试宇量升光开发的设备，计划在通过验证后于2027年实现产线整合。《金融时报》将该设备与ASML 2008年上市的Twinscan NXT:1950i进行对比，认为其设计比ASML目前销售的设备落后约15年。宇量升光2022年在上海成立，注册资本10亿元人民币（约1.49亿美元），据信截至去年底已向晶圆厂交付三台光刻机进行测试，但该消息未获官方确认。

国产化进程仍面临核心瓶颈。该设备所需的许多关键零部件仍依赖从日本进口，这些本土供应商的交付延误正是2026年产量被限制在约5台的原因。因此，2027年20台的目标颇具雄心，它假设届时将建成一个目前尚未形成的国产零部件供应链，且进口部件仍处在未来任何一轮出口管制的影响范围之内。

从行业整体国产化率来看，光刻环节最为薄弱。SMEE目前最先进的量产产品仍是SSA600系列——一款90纳米级干式ArF扫描光刻机，已于去年5月投入量产。该公司2023年宣布的28纳米级SSA/800浸没式设备从未实际部署，官方媒体关于其成功研发的报道也在发布后不久被删除。去年12月，SMEE获得一份约1.1亿元人民币（1600万美元）的政府单一来源合同，供应一款规格为110纳米分辨率和15纳米套刻精度的KrF扫描光刻机，这在一定程度上反映了其当前量产能力的真实水平。

据中国半导体行业协会数据，2025年国产设备占中国晶圆厂采购额的35%，超过了北京设定的30%目标，较三年前的约10%大幅提升。刻蚀和薄膜沉积设备的国产化率已突破40%，量测设备达到25%，而光刻仅为18%，且大部分集中在成熟制程和封装领域。自2025年底起，新建晶圆厂产能被要求至少一半设备实现本土采购，这一强制规定为新光刻机提供了确定的客户基础，无论其最终性能规格如何。

国产设备企业的整体表现同样值得关注。北方华创凭借2025年销售额成为全球第五大芯片设备制造商，仅次于ASML、应用材料、泛林半导体和东京电子，并超越KLA。该公司2025年前三季度营收达271.4亿元人民币（40亿美元），而2020年全年仅为60.5亿元人民币（5.89亿美元），订单积压已排至2027年，并首次开始布局光刻设备研发。中微公司2025年营收和净利润均增长超过30%，清洗设备专业厂商盛美半导体2025财年营收达9.013亿美元，预计2026年最高可达11.8亿美元。

与华为关系密切的深圳新凯来在2025年3月的SEMICON China上展示了约30款设备，涵盖刻蚀、沉积、量测和测试领域，据报道截至2025年9月估值达650亿元人民币（96.3亿美元），在手订单超过100亿元人民币（14.8亿美元）。美国已于2024年12月将其列入实体清单。

然而，行业领导层对现状的评估远不如数据所显示的那般乐观。今年3月，中芯国际联合创始人王阳元、长江存储、北方华创及华大九天负责人联合将中国设备行业描述为"小、散、弱"，呼吁国家层面推动整合，大基金三期475亿美元资金正被导向光刻和EDA领域。埃斯纳这家将宇量升光和SMEE团队合并为单一国有实体的企业，正是这一整合压力下的首个产物。据SEMI数据，中国2024年在晶圆厂设备上创纪录地支出495亿美元，即便2025年有所回调，到2027年仍将是全球最大买家。

在EUV光刻领域，路透社2025年12月的一项调查报道（被称为中国的"曼哈顿计划"）披露，在深圳一个高安全性实验室内，一套可运行的EUV光源原型机已于2025年初完工。该设备能产生EUV光子，但尚未完成晶圆曝光。据报道，该项目有超过3000名研究人员参与，华为担任协调角色，SMEE负责系统集成。两个团队正在竞逐光源方案：北京航空航天大学教授林楠（2015至2021年间曾在ASML工作）领导的固体激光等离子体方案，目前转换效率为3.42%，而商业化可行所需约为5.5%；哈尔滨工业大学赵永鹏领导的激光辅助放电等离子体团队，其EUV输出功率已达约100瓦，而ASML生产型光源的输出功率约为600瓦。北京设定的目标是在2028年前实现该设备产出芯片，但路透社消息人士认为2030年更为现实。另有报道描述了一个围绕截获的Cymer光源逆向工程搭建的原型机，同样未产出任何结果。2025年3月中国媒体流传的华为EUV试产和2026年量产的早前说法，从未得到任何一手信源证实。清华大学的加速器基SSMB方案——需要周长100至150米的同步加速器——目前仍是学术项目。

出口管制方面，4月初在参众两院提出的MATCH法案不仅将禁止向中芯国际、华为、华虹、长鑫存储和长江存储销售浸没式DUV设备，还将禁止对已安装设备的维护服务，并给予荷兰和日本150天的政策协调期。该法案目前仍是提案而非法律，但服务限制将直接打击支撑中国目前所有先进芯片产出的已安装ASML设备基础——包括华为麒麟9030中所用中芯国际N+3节点。中国晶圆厂已在为此做准备，通过第三方工程师和灰市零部件以"弗兰肯斯坦"方式拼修老旧ASML设备。ASML的中国敞口正按计划收缩：中国占其系统销售额的比重从2024年的41%（去年为33%）降至目前的20%，尽管该公司7月已将全年营收指引上调至430至450亿欧元。同样，应用材料预计本财年中国收入将损失6亿至7.1亿美元。

最终，三个关键标志将检验中国国产DUV计划究竟是真正的竞争对手，还是又一次国家批准的虚张声势：首要标志是埃斯纳设备在中芯国际、华虹或长鑫存储产出经过验证的生产晶圆，并公布吞吐量和良率数据；其次是2027年能否交付接近20台设备的计划数量；第三是深圳EUV原型机能否在北京设定的2028年目标之前完成首片晶圆曝光。

history.title: At least 37 people arrested in 2026 so far for protesting against data centers, most for breaking 'petty rules' — most taken into custody acted peacefully
history.description: Data center protesters are getting arrested for minor infractions, yet they continue pushing back against these projects. Aside from the arrests, there's also at least 12 instances (probably more) where the police were called to intervene between politicians and protesters.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Although the majority of Americans oppose data centers going up in their backyards, several local governments still support similar developments as they believe that these will bring investments and opportunities for their constituents. However, the passionate but peaceful resistance of some people has resulted in their arrests, with Futurism reporting that 37 regular people have been arrested so far this year.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)Photonics and high-speed data movement is the next big AI bottleneckThe data center cooling state of playMassive AI data center buildouts are squeezing energy suppliesUltra Ethernet: The data center interconnection of tomorrowWhat’s more interesting is the wide demographic diversity of those who have been detained and charged. The two arrests Tom’s Hardware previously reported on included a farmer who went a few seconds over the allotted speaking time during a town hall meeting in Oklahoma discussing an AI data center project and a teacher who was dragged out of a community meeting in Kansas for clapping after a speaker finished giving their statement opposing another similar development. The protesters also crossed ideologies and party lines — the only common thing among them was the fact that they were concerned about the impact of a data center in their community.The publication also noted that there were 12 other instances where the police were called because of a confrontation between politicians and protesting individuals. One example of this is when police intervened after a Utah senator got physical and slapped the phone out of a reporter’s hand, who was only there to cover the harassment by anti-data center protesters against his business.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: “In my opinion, I was kicked out to prove a point that the law is on their side and if people continue to try and express themselves and speak, they will also be intimidated or arrested by law enforcement,” Pablo Payan, a maintenance manager who was arrested in Indiana after he refused to identify himself on the record, told Fox32. “So, I think it was a flex of power.”Data centers have become a hot topic among the American public recently, especially as there have been widespread reports of these developments causing massive increases in electricity costs, negative impacts on the local water quality, 24/7 noise pollution, among other issues. The federal government has taken steps to reduce some of the impact through its “ratepayer protection pledge,” which includes AI hyperscalers, utility companies, data center operators, and even state governors. However, some experts say that this is just a promise that has no legal bearing, meaning companies necessarily don’t need to follow it. You may like 142 AI data center protests staged in 42 states as public opposition increases 70% of Americans oppose data centers near their homes, now less popular than nuclear power plants AI data center bans are rapidly multiplying across the US Even though a few jurisdictions are pushing forward with data center projects despite local opposition, there are also some local and state governments that have paused their development. These include multiple Tennessee counties, Seattle, Washington, which is home to the headquarters of Microsoft and Amazon, and the State of New York. Most of them said they will use the one-year delay to study the effects of data center developments and how to best mitigate against them. One Pennsylvania town even took a different approach by listing 43 specific demands for a proposed data center, which its developer allegedly shot down as “too difficult.”This is likely what made these protesters emboldened in their fight against data centers — the fact that other communities have successfully lobbied against data center developments means that they can push back, too.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.

history.descriptionZh:
尽管多数美国民众反对数据中心建在自家后院，但部分地方政府仍支持此类项目，认为能带来投资和就业机会。这种分歧导致激烈的民间抵抗，据Futurism报道，今年已有37名普通民众因抗议AI数据中心建设而被捕。Tom's Hardware此前报道的两起逮捕案例颇具代表性：一位俄克拉何马州的农民在市政厅会议上就AI数据中心项目发言时超时数秒即被逮捕；堪萨斯州一位教师在社区会议上因鼓掌反对该项目被拖出会场。被捕者的身份涵盖了维修经理、农民、教师等不同职业，政治立场也横跨意识形态和党派界限，唯一的共同点是他们都担忧数据中心对社区的影响。此外，还有12起冲突事件报警处理，如犹他州一名参议员在反数据中心抗议者骚扰其企业时，动手打落了前来采访记者的手机。

数据中心之所以成为美国公众热议焦点，主要源于其对当地电费、水质和噪音的负面影响。大规模AI数据中心建设正在挤压能源供应，冷却系统和高速数据传输也面临瓶颈。联邦政府虽推出“纳税人保护承诺”以缓解冲击，涵盖AI超大规模企业、公用事业公司、数据中心运营商甚至州长，但专家指出这仅是政治承诺，不具备法律约束力，企业未必需要遵守。

尽管部分辖区不顾反对继续推进项目，也有多个地方选择暂停开发，包括田纳西州多个县、微软和亚马逊总部所在地西雅图以及纽约州。这些地区大多利用一年的暂停期研究数据中心开发的影响及应对策略。宾夕法尼亚州一个小镇甚至对拟建数据中心提出43项具体要求，但开发者认为“过于困难”而拒绝。正是这些成功抵制案例鼓舞了抗议者，他们认为只要发声就可能改变局面。这场由AI数据中心的公共影响引发的公民抗命浪潮，正逐渐演变为一场跨越城乡、阶级和党派的社会运动。

history.title: Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11 Review: A good display meets a low-power RTX 5060
history.description: The Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11 pairs an RTX 5060, 144 Hz display, and excellent upgradeability with a comfortable keyboard, but its low-power GPU configuration and outdated CPU leave it struggling against rivals at the same price.
history.content: The Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11 has the right idea to compete with the best budget gaming laptops: skip the flashy design extras and focus on the hardware that matters. Its RTX 5060 graphics, 144 Hz IPS display, solid keyboard, and generous internal upgrade options give budget-strapped gamers plenty to like on paper. The reality is that this configuration is compromised in the area that matters most: gaming performance. Its RTX 5060 is held back by a 65W power limit and the CPU is several generations old, allowing rival machines in the same price range to post stronger results. The LOQ is usable and practical, but at this price, it needs stronger performance to stand out.Design of the Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11 Aptly named, the LOQ Essentials 15 embraces a no-frills design. Aside from LOQ branding on the lid, there’s little here meant to catch the eye, which is fitting for a laptop that’s intended to deliver performance at the lowest possible cost. Lenovo reserves premium materials and styling for its Legion gaming laptops.Fortunately, the budget considerations are mostly aesthetic, as the LOQ’s plastic chassis feels solid and has the durability you’d expect for daily home or school use. Its 0.97-inch thick profile and 5.07-pound weight don’t make it a great traveling companion are in line with competing laptops like Acer's Nitro V 16S AI, Asus’ TUF Gaming F16, and MSI's Cyborg 15. The latter is the lightest in the group, at 4.36 pounds.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Image 1 of 2 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 2 View Original Image 2 of 2 View Original Lenovo’s port selection is practical: one USB-C port (10 Gbps), two USB-A ports (5 Gbps), an audio jack, Ethernet, and HDMI. You won't get truly high-speed ports like USB4/Thunderbolt 4 at this price. The Intel AX203 Wi-Fi 6 card is another example of this laptop's economical focus, though it shouldn't hold users back. Image 1 of 3 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 3 View Original Image 2 of 3 View Original Image 3 of 3 View Original Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11 Specifications Swipe to scroll horizontally CPU Intel Core i7-13650HX Graphics Nvidia RTX 5060 (8GB GDDR7, 1,455 MHz boost, 65 W maximum graphics power) Memory 16GB DDR5-4800 RAM (1x 16GB) Storage 512GB SSD (WD PC SN5000S) Display 15.6-inch, 1920 x 1080, IPS, anti-glare, 144 Hz Networking Intel Wi-Fi 6 AX203, Bluetooth 5.4 Ports USB-C (10 Gbps), 2x USB-A (5 Gbps), audio, Ethernet, HDMI Camera 720p Battery 60 Wh Power Adapter 135 W (barrel connector) Operating System Windows 11 Home Dimensions (WxDxH) 14.22 x 10.06 x 0.97 inches (361 x 256 x 25 mm) Weight 5.07 pounds (2.3 kg) Price (as configured) $1,269.99 Today's best Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11 deals No price informationCheck AmazonWe check over 250 million products every day for the best pricesGaming and Graphics on the Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11We evaluated the LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11 with a Core i7-13650HX processor, RTX 5060 graphics (65W), and 16GB of single-channel DDR5-4800 RAM. The processor is several years old though still packs a punch, with six Performance cores.Playing 007 First Light at 1080p with medium lighting settings, post effects on, and DLSS set to balanced, the LOQ produced playable frame rates, ranging from the mid-50s to low-70s FPS depending on the scene. The experience was never poor, but it lacked the fluidity I expected from a laptop carrying Nvidia's latest midrange GPU.Our benchmark comparison lineup consists of Acer's Nitro V 16S AI (Ryzen 7 260, RTX 5060 85W, $1,299.99 when tested), Asus' TUF Gaming F16 (Core i7-14650HX, RTX 5050 115W, $1,199.99), and MSI's Cyborg 15 C13WE (Core i5-13420H, RTX 5050 70W, $1,219.99).Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Image 1 of 6 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 6 View Original Image 2 of 6 View Original Image 3 of 6 View Original Image 4 of 6 View Original Image 5 of 6 View Original Image 6 of 6 View Original Overall, the LOQ’s results were disappointing. With a 65W power limit, its RTX 5060 simply doesn't deliver the level of performance buyers might expect from the badge. It was routinely outperformed by the TUF Gaming F16 using an RTX 5050, while Acer's higher-powered RTX 5060 laptop also finished comfortably ahead. The result is a gaming laptop that works well enough but struggles to justify its price when similarly priced alternatives make better use of comparable hardware.In Shadow of the Tomb Raider at the Highest detail preset, the LOQ’s 88 FPS only outpaced the Cyborg (82 FPS), while the Asus (95 FPS) and Acer (98 FPS) both pulled ahead. This story repeated in Far Cry 6 – with 75 FPS, the LOQ trailed Acer (82 FPS) and Asus (90 FPS), though it was within a few FPS of those units in Red Dead Redemption 2. The LOQ’s only real victory was Cyberpunk 2077, where it achieved 38 FPS, with the Acer (32 FPS) trailing. The LOQ was one of two laptops tested with Forza Horizon 3, where it predictably had no trouble outgunning the Cyborg, 58 FPS to 51 FPS.To stress-test gaming laptops, we run 15 loops of the Metro Exodus stress test at RTX settings to simulate half an hour of gaming. The LOQ demonstrated stable performance throughout the test, averaging 59.79 FPS without a variance of more than one FPS across runs. During the test, the Core i7-13650HX ran at an average frequency of 2.73 GHz while the RTX 5060 averaged 1,919 MHz.Productivity Performance on the Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11Our LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11 is built around a Core i7-13650HX, 16GB of RAM, and a 512GB SSD. Image 1 of 3 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 3 View Original Image 2 of 3 View Original Image 3 of 3 View Original Throughout our testing, the LOQ's outdated CPU struggled against the newer silicon in the competition, only consistently outpacing the Cyborg with its equally dated Core i5-13420H. In the multi-core portion of Geekbench, the LOQ's score of 11,300 was well behind the Ryzen 7 260-powered Acer (12,837) and couldn't touch the Core i7-14650HX-powered Asus (15,013). The Asus also dominated Handbrake, completing that test in 3 minutes and 33 seconds compared to the LOQ's 4:35.The LOQ's average speed of 136 MBps in our 25GB file transfer is abnormal, but it also occurred on other drive benchmarks, though I never noticed any issues in loading games. The drive is a WD PC SN5000S using QLC.Display on the Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11Lenovo didn't cut too many corners with the LOQ's display. The 15.6-inch IPS panel pairs a smooth 144 Hz refresh rate with an anti-glare finish that minimizes reflections. While the 1920 x 1080 resolution isn't especially sharp by 2026 standards, it isn’t too hard for the RTX 5060 to drive in today’s games.Watching X2: X-Men United and playing 007 First Light, the LOQ’s display stood out as one that’s better than typical budget laptop fare. Colors have enough punch to make game environments feel lively, and enough contrast to give darker scenes reasonable depth. Brightness is just adequate – the panel is best suited for indoor use and can't compete with the significantly brighter screen in Acer's Nitro V 16S AI. Still, for gaming, streaming, and everyday use, the LOQ's display is one of its better attributes. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Covering 86.1% of DCI-P3, the LOQ’s display proved more colorful than the Acer (77.4%) and effectively tied the others. Its 290-nit peak brightness was on par with the Asus (298 nits) and brighter than the MSI (233 nits) but not nearly as bright as the Acer (392 nits).Keyboard and Touchpad on the Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11Lenovo’s keyboard offers an ample 1.3 mm of travel for comfortable typing sessions. Its two-level white backlighting provides excellent visibility in low light. The number pad isn’t quite full-size but offers the expected layout. In MonkeyType, I reached 122 words per minute with 99% accuracy on the first try.The touchpad is also well-designed, with a comfortably-sized surface and quiet physical clicks. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Audio on the Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11The LOQ's twin 2W speakers produce acceptable sound for a laptop. Bass is lacking, but the sound is clear enough to pick out footsteps and shell cases dropping in games. Overall, the setup works for casual gaming.The included Nahimic app is essential for sound quality – without it, the speakers are tinny and dull. The Music preset with bass and treble boost works well all around. The Smart preset also gets the job done; my ears didn't detect much of a difference versus the Music preset. The Movie preset's virtual surround adds a hollowness that I find unnatural.Upgradeability of the Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11Getting inside the LOQ is somewhat tricky. Removing the Philips-head screws is straightforward – they’re fortunately all the same size – but the bottom panel sits flush with the chassis edges, with no obvious entry points. I created one using my thumb to push in one of the rear chassis corners, which created a gap for my plastic pry tool.Upgrade prospects are excellent, with two DDR5 SODIMM slots and two SSD slots, one M.2 2280 and one M.2 2242. The 512GB SSD in our model is M.2 2242 format and installed in the M.2 2280 slot. The M.2 2230 wireless card and the battery are also replaceable. Image 1 of 2 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 2 View Original Image 2 of 2 View Original Battery Life on the Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11Our battery testing consists of web browsing, running OpenGL tests, and streaming videos with the screen at 150 nits while connected to Wi-Fi. The LOQ's runtime of 4 hours and 54 minutes is short even for a gaming laptop, with the Asus lasting about two hours longer. Acer's Nitro completely outclassed it, lasting 10 hours and 17 minutes. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Heat on the Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11We measure laptop surface temperatures while running the Metro Exodus stress test. The LOQ's peak temperatures were 108 degrees Fahrenheit (F) between the G and H keys while the touchpad was 79 F. The highest temperature was 112 F on the bottom near the cooling fan exhaust. Internally, the Core i7-13650HX measured 70 degrees Celsius (C) while the RTX 5060 was 66 C.The LOQ’s fan noise is noticeable while gaming, but is no louder than other entry-level gaming laptops I’ve tested. Its speakers are easily loud enough to be heard over the fans.Webcam on the Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11Lenovo's webcam is a basic 720p model with a soft focus. It handles lighting reasonably well – a lamp behind me wasn't blown out – but detail is lacking and there's considerable grain. There's no physical shutter, but you'll find an e-shutter switch on the right edge.Software and Warranty on the Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11The LOQ includes two main apps. Legion Space shows component readouts like CPU speed and temperature, plus power profile toggles between Performance, Quiet, Balanced, and Custom. The app can also auto-disable the Windows key and auto-close specified apps when games are launched, and prioritize network traffic to apps you specify. An aim assist feature puts a crosshair in the center of the screen. The app also provides access to the Lenovo community and can be a game library.The Vantage app is familiar across Lenovo laptops for support services, troubleshooting utilities, and system updates. System settings include battery smart charging (limits charge to 80% to extend battery lifespan). The app also has a security advisor that verifies anti-virus and firewalls are active and tells you if a Wi-Fi network is safe. The app contains upsells for Lenovo’s identity protection, system recovery, and performance tuneup subscription services.Lenovo backs the LOQ with a one-year warranty.Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11 ConfigurationsWe tested the LOQ equipped with a Core i7-13650HX processor, RTX 5060 graphics card, 16GB of DDR5-4800 single-channel RAM, and a 512GB SSD, retailing for $1,269.99 at Best Buy. It was not yet available directly from Lenovo at the time of this review.An even more basic spec with a Core i5-13450HX and RTX 5050 is listed on Lenovo's site as "coming soon" but wasn’t at the time of publishing. All configurations include a 1920 x 1080 IPS display with a 144 Hz refresh rate and Windows 11 Home.Bottom LineLenovo’s LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11 is a reminder that spec sheets don’t tell the whole story. While it delivers an RTX 5060 and a 144 Hz display for a competitive price, its conservative GPU power limits and older platform leave it trailing rivals in real-world performance. Though it gets many fundamentals right -- its display, keyboard, and upgradeability are all solid – it’s ultimately a serviceable gaming laptop rather than a competitive one. At this price, Acer’s Nitro V 16S AI is a stronger value.

history.titleZh: Lenovo LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11 Review: A good display meets a low-power RTX 5060
history.descriptionZh:
联想LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11是一款定位入门级预算游戏本的产品，其设计思路非常明确：舍弃花哨的外观元素，将成本集中在核心硬件上。从纸面配置看，它搭载了英伟达RTX 5060显卡、144Hz IPS高刷屏、手感扎实的键盘以及丰富的内部扩展位，确实对预算有限的玩家颇具吸引力。然而，实际测试揭示了一个关键问题——这台笔记本在最核心的游戏性能上做出了妥协，导致其真实表现远低于RTX 5060这一型号所应有的水平，在同价位竞品中处于劣势。

## 设计：实用至上，用料俭省

LOQ Essentials 15的外观与“Essentials”之名相符，采用全塑料机身，除顶盖上的LOQ标识外几乎没有任何装饰元素。联想将高端材质与设计语言留给了Legion系列，因此这台机器在视觉上非常朴素。不过，塑料机身的做工并不廉价，整体结构坚固，足以应对日常家用或校园场景。机身厚度0.97英寸（约24.6毫米），重量5.07磅（约2.3公斤），与宏碁Nitro V 16S AI、华硕TUF Gaming F16以及微星Cyborg 15等竞品相当，其中Cyborg 15最轻，为4.36磅。

接口方面以实用性为主：一个USB-C（10Gbps）、两个USB-A（5Gbps）、音频插孔、RJ45以太网口和HDMI。该价位自然没有USB4或雷电4这类高速端口。无线网络采用英特尔AX203 Wi-Fi 6网卡，同样是经济型选择，但性能足以满足日常使用。

## 核心配置与性能瓶颈

本次评测的LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11具体配置如下：

| 部件 | 规格 |
|------|------|
| CPU | Intel Core i7-13650HX（6个性能核） |
| GPU | Nvidia RTX 5060（8GB GDDR7，最高1455MHz，最大功率65W） |
| 内存 | 16GB DDR5-4800（单通道，1×16GB） |
| 存储 | 512GB SSD（WD PC SN5000S，QLC） |
| 屏幕 | 15.6英寸IPS，1920×1080，144Hz，防眩光 |
| 电池 | 60Wh |
| 电源 | 135W（圆口） |
| 价格 | 1269.99美元（百思买） |

**性能受限的核心原因**在于GPU功耗墙设定。RTX 5060的功率上限被限制在65W，远低于同类笔记本常见的85W甚至更高。这意味着GPU无法发挥其全部性能潜力。同时，Core i7-13650HX虽然拥有6个性能核，但已是几代前的产品，在CPU密集型任务中明显落后于搭载最新处理器的竞品。此外，单通道DDR5内存也进一步限制了CPU访存带宽，对游戏帧率产生负面影响。

### 游戏性能实测

在《007：First Light》中，1080p中等画质、后处理开启、DLSS设为平衡档，帧率在50多到70多FPS之间波动，虽然可玩，但远未达到RTX 5060应有的流畅度。与竞品对比更显弱势：

- 《Shadow of the Tomb Raider》最高画质：LOQ为88FPS，微星Cyborg 15（RTX 5050 70W）为82FPS，华硕TUF F16（RTX 5050 115W）95FPS，宏碁Nitro V 16S AI（RTX 5060 85W）98FPS。
- 《Far Cry 6》：LOQ为75FPS，宏碁82FPS，华硕90FPS，微星未列出。
- 《Red Dead Redemption 2》中与竞品差距较小，仅差几帧。
- 唯一胜出的是《Cyberpunk 2077》：LOQ达到38FPS，而宏碁只有32FPS（可能是DLSS设置差异或测试版本不同所致）。
- 《Forza Horizon 3》中LOQ以58FPS对51FPS击败微星Cyborg。

在《Metro Exodus》15轮RTX压力测试中，LOQ表现稳定，平均59.79FPS，各轮间帧率波动不超过1FPS，说明散热和功耗管理平稳。测试期间CPU平均频率2.73GHz，GPU平均频率1919MHz。

### 生产力性能

Geekbench多核测试中，LOQ得分11300，落后于搭载锐龙7 260的宏碁（12837），更远低于搭载酷睿i7-14650HX的华硕（15013）。Handbrake视频转码用时4分35秒，而华硕仅用3分33秒。25GB文件传输平均速度136MB/s，处于异常较低水平，但在游戏加载中并未察觉明显问题。这与其采用QLC颗粒的WD SN5000S SSD有关，属于成本控制的体现。

## 显示与输入体验

LOQ的屏幕是少数亮点之一。15.6英寸IPS面板支持144Hz刷新率和防眩光涂层，虽然1080p分辨率在如今不算高，但对RTX 5060而言反而更容易驱动。实测色彩表现良好，覆盖86.1%的DCI-P3色域，优于宏碁的77.4%，与其他竞品持平。峰值亮度290尼特，与华硕的298尼特相当，高于微星的233尼特，但低于宏碁的392尼特。观影和游戏时色彩饱和度足够，暗部对比度合理，不过亮度仅适合室内使用。

键盘提供1.3mm键程，打字体验舒适，两档白色背光在低光环境下清晰可见。测试中首次输入达到122字/分钟，准确率99%。触摸板尺寸适中，物理点击安静且响应准确。

## 音频、可升级性与电池

内置双2W扬声器音质中规中矩，缺乏低音，但能清晰分辨游戏中的脚步声和弹壳落地声。必须安装Nahimic音效软件，否则声音会变得单薄刺耳；Music预设（低音和高音增强）效果最佳，Movie预设的虚拟环绕声则显得空洞不自然。

内部可升级性令人满意。打开底盖需要一点技巧（螺丝统一规格，但底盖与机身贴合紧密，需用拇指在后角撬开缝隙），内部有两个DDR5 SODIMM内存插槽和两个M.2 SSD插槽（一个2280规格，一个2242规格）。本机标配的512GB SSD为M.2 2242，安装在2280槽位内。无线网卡和电池均可更换。

电池续航是明显短板。在150尼特亮度下进行网页浏览、OpenGL测试和视频流播放，仅坚持4小时54分钟，远短于正常使用预期。华硕TUF F16比它长2小时左右，而宏碁Nitro V 16S AI更长达10小时17分钟，几乎是前者的两倍。

## 散热与噪声

在Metro Exodus压力测试中，键盘中央（G和H键之间）最高温度108华氏度（约42°C），触摸板79华氏度（约26°C），底部靠近散热出风口处最高112华氏度（约44°C）。内部CPU温度70°C，GPU为66°C，散热系统完全能压制硬件。游戏时风扇噪音明显，但与同类入门游戏本相当，扬声器音量足以盖过风扇声。

## 摄像头、软件与保修

720p摄像头画质一般，对焦偏软，细节不足，但曝光处理尚可，没有过度过曝。无物理隐私遮挡，但机身右侧提供电子摄像头开关。

预装两款主要软件：Legion Space和Vantage。Legion Space提供CPU频率、温度等部件读数，以及性能/静音/均衡/自定义四种电源模式切换，还可以在游戏启动时自动禁用Windows键、关闭指定应用、优先网络流量，并提供屏幕准星辅助功能。Vantage则负责系统更新、故障诊断、电池智能充电（可限制充电至80%以延长寿命），以及安全顾问等功能，但绑定了一些付费订阅服务（如身份保护、系统恢复、性能调优）。整机提供一年质保。

## 结论与购买建议

联想LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11深刻揭示了一个道理：参数表不等于实际体验。它确实以有竞争力的价格提供了RTX 5060和144Hz高刷屏，但保守的GPU功耗墙和落后的CPU平台使它在实际性能上落后于对手。虽然屏幕、键盘和可升级性等基本功做得扎实，但作为一台游戏本，它只能算“可用”，而非“能打”。官方定价1269.99美元，在这个价位上，宏碁Nitro V 16S AI以更高的GPU功耗、更强的CPU和将近两倍的电池续航，提供了明显更优的综合价值。对于追求游戏帧率和性价比的玩家而言，LOQ Essentials 15 Gen 11不是最好的选择。

history.title: 16GB GPUs and 8-core CPUs officially become the most popular configs on Steam — Latest hardware survey shows modern gaming's growing hunger for more resources
history.description: For the first time in Steam history, 8-core CPUs have overtaken 6-core CPUs and GPUs with 16GB of VRAM have overtaken 8GB GPUs. Even though the hardware survey doesn't represent everyone, it still indicates a paradigm shift for the mainstream market.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 7 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Wirth's law dictates that software becomes slower more rapidly than hardware gets faster. That logic can explain why games today look mostly the same as they did a decade ago, yet require a lot more resources to run comfortably. That sentiment is now reflected in Steam's latest hardware survey as well, where 8-core CPUs have overtaken 6-core CPUs for the first time ever, and GPUs with 16GB of VRAM have become the most common on the platform.The results for July 2026 show that 16GB GPUs now represent 25.9% of all Steam users, just edging out 8GB GPUs that sit at 25.32% adoption. In June, 16GB GPUs were at 24.50%, so they gained 1.4 points in a month, while 8GB GPUs lost 0.32 points in the same time. This is the first month in the storefront's history where 8GB of VRAM is no longer considered enough, closing the book on this debate in a rather definitive way. Keep in mind that these numbers combine all Steam instances across Windows, Linux, and Mac. (Image credit: Future)When it comes to processors, the need to move away from 6-core chips hasn't really been of concern since they're still enough for gaming. It was not long ago that Intel was refreshing the same quad-core CPUs year after year until AMD's resurgence pushed the industry out of stagnation. This is evident by the fact that 4-core CPUs still enjoy a 13.2% share of the pie. But today, it's clear that the shift has begun as Steam's most recent data shows 27.85% of the userbase is rocking 8-core CPUs, while 27.52% have 6-core CPUs.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Once again, it's the first time this precedent has shifted as 8-core chips became 0.32% more popular this month compared to last, the most of any config, while 6-core chips lost 0.12% of their adoption. The extreme popularity of X3D chips for gaming is partly responsible, since the 5800X3D, then the 7800X3D, and now, the 9800X3D, all feature 8 cores and 16 threads. Intel's hybrid architecture makes it so that pretty much none of its midrange or high-end chips have exactly 8 cores (though many have 8 P-cores). (Image credit: Future)The obsolescence of 6-core CPUs and 8GB GPUs is not a sudden event; we've been witnessing this decline since at least last year, when their numbers first started to dwindle. Sales figures from across the world, multiple times, have shown how customers heavily prefer to buy 16GB versions of the same GPUs that also have an 8GB model. Such a small memory pool is simply not enough for modern games, especially since they've begun relying on ray tracing as a requirement now. You may like AMD reaches 45% CPU share in latest Steam Hardware Survey for Windows gaming PCs Gaming on the 4GB Radeon RX 6500 XT and GTX 1650 Super in 2026 Radeon RX 9070 XT finally appears in Steam Hardware Survey "What Andy gives, Bill takes away" is a niche adage in the tech space that referred to Microsoft's bloatware outpacing hardware advancements made by Intel back in the 90s. It still holds true today, but it's better combined with May's Law — the idea that the abundance of silicon will make developers lazy, such that they'll stop optimizing their code to its fullest potential. Of course, this is a bit ironic considering we're in a component crisis at the moment, where soaring memory and storage prices are now coming to bite back said developers.The consumers are not stuck with the debt of years of inefficiency. If you still have an 8GB GPU today, like the 5060 Ti, there's a high chance you won't be able to play upcoming modern games smoothly, even if the core itself remains perfectly capable. Anyhow, the Steam Hardware Survey doesn't represent the entire market, obviously, but it's a good indication of mainstream trends. They show that the RTX 3060 is still the most popular current-gen card in the world, while the RTX 5070 is climbing the charts fast. history.titleZh: 16GB GPUs and 8-core CPUs officially become the most popular configs on Steam — Latest hardware survey shows modern gaming's growing hunger for more resources
history.descriptionZh:
随着游戏与软件对硬件资源的需求持续攀升，Steam最新一期（2026年7月）硬件调查结果揭示了两个历史性转折：8核CPU首次在用户占比上超越6核CPU，而拥有16GB显存的显卡则首次取代8GB显卡成为平台主流配置。这一变化不仅印证了Wirth定律——软件变慢的速度往往快于硬件变快的速度，也标志着持续多年的“8GB显存是否够用”争论终于落下帷幕。

从具体数据来看，16GB显存GPU目前在Steam用户中的占比达到25.9%，略高于8GB显存的25.32%。仅在一个月内，16GB显卡的份额就增长了1.4个百分点，而8GB显卡则下降了0.32个百分点。这是Steam平台历史上首次出现8GB显存不再被视为“够用”的月份，具有指标性意义。该统计涵盖了Windows、Linux和macOS等所有平台的Steam实例。

处理器方面同样出现了历史性变化：8核CPU份额达到27.85%，首次超越6核CPU的27.52%。其中8核芯片的份额环比增长0.32个百分点，是所有配置中增幅最大的；而6核芯片则下降了0.12个百分点。值得注意的是，4核CPU仍保有13.2%的份额，说明旧配置的淘汰并非一蹴而就，但主流天平已经明确倾斜。

造成这一趋势的推手之一，是AMD X3D系列游戏处理器的持续火爆。从5800X3D、7800X3D到最新的9800X3D，这些备受玩家追捧的芯片均采用8核16线程设计。相比之下，Intel的混合架构使得其中高端产品很少恰好包含8个完整核心（许多型号拥有8个P核但加上E核后总数并非8），这也在一定程度上促成了8核配置的快速普及。

显存容量的升级同样不是突然发生的。早在去年，8GB显卡的份额就已开始持续下滑，而全球多份销售数据也反复表明，即便同一款显卡同时提供8GB和16GB版本，绝大多数消费者也会倾向于选择16GB。这一变化背后是游戏图形技术的现实需求：现代3A大作越来越多地将光线追踪作为基本要求，而光追对显存容量的消耗远高于传统光栅化渲染。小容量显存不仅会限制纹理和几何细节的加载，还容易在高分辨率或高画质设定下出现帧率骤降甚至卡顿。

这种“软件吞噬硬件进步”的现象并非新概念。科技界流传已久的“Andy and Bill”定律——Intel CEO安迪·格鲁夫（Andy Grove）带来的硬件性能提升，总是被微软联合创始人比尔·盖茨（Bill Gates）的软件膨胀所抵消——至今依然适用。而在AI芯片与半导体产业高度发达的今天，它又与"May定律"形成交汇：硅资源的极大丰富会让开发者变得“懒惰”，逐渐放弃对代码和游戏引擎进行深度优化，转而依赖更强的硬件来兜底。讽刺的是，当前全球正面临内存和存储芯片的价格飙升，这种“资源无限”的假设正被现实打破，长期累积的效率债最终可能转嫁到消费者和开发者自身头上。

对于普通玩家而言，这一趋势的实际影响相当直接：如果你目前仍在使用8GB显存的显卡，即便是像RTX 5060 Ti这样核心性能尚且不错的型号，在未来的新游戏中也很可能难以保证流畅体验。显存容量已不再只是“多开高分辨率材质”的锦上添花，而是决定游戏能否正常运行的关键门槛。

当然，Steam硬件调查并不能代表整个PC市场，但它无疑是观察主流玩家硬件偏好的最佳风向标。目前，英伟达的RTX 3060依然是全球最流行的当前一代显卡，而RTX 5070的排名正在快速攀升。相比之下，AMD和Intel在GPU榜单上的存在感仍然有限，只能算作“荣誉提名”。整体来看，8核CPU与16GB显存的普及，象征着一个旧世代的结束和新性能基准的确立——未来几年，这一配置组合很可能成为玩家升级的起点而非终点。

history.title: China cracks down on copycat chip designs with new regulations and penalties — new guidelines enforce originality and independent development
history.description: China tightens legal protections for domestically developed chip layout designs by raising originality requirements and strengthening infringement penalties.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 3 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter China has revised its regulations concerning protection of integrated circuit (IC) layout designs developed domestically. The new regulations are intended to make it harder for Chinese companies to obtain legal protection for copied chip designs by tightening originality requirements, registration procedures, and infringement remedies, Reuters reports. As a result, it will get harder for underperforming China-based companies to copy ICs developed by their more successful rivals. Meanwhile, Chinese chipmakers will be allowed to produce their designs in Taiwan or South Korea.Go deeper with TH Premium: Chipmaking (Image credit: tsmc)A deeper look at the chipmaking supply chainTSMC's $165 billion U.S. investments examinedChina reportedly reverse-engineers EUV toolChina bets on DUV, as EUV blockade reshapes chipmakingThe amended regulations apply to physical chip layout designs that define how circuit elements are arranged on silicon and represent a substantial amount of engineering work, including for companies that specialize in chip design rather than manufacturing. To qualify for legal protection of their IC layouts, applications must now demonstrate that the layout was independently developed, formally attest that the design is original, and specify which parts of the layout constitute their own creative contribution (perhaps to give authorities an idea about which were licensed or obtained from open sources). As a result, authorities will be able to filter out weak claims and distinguish companies with strong technological capabilities. Furthermore, they will also be able to determine whether a particular chip was designed and built in China, or its alleged developer obtained its product elsewhere and attempts to disguise it as a 'Made in China' silicon.The new rules also strengthen enforcement. From mid-October and onwards, in infringement disputes, courts may determine compensation based either on losses suffered by the rights holder or profits earned by the infringing party. Punitive damages will also become an option. In addition, the regulations clarify procedures for licensing, transferring, or using IC layout-design rights as collateral. Organizations that develop protected layouts are also required to provide reasonable rewards and payments to personnel responsible for creating those designs.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Chinese policymakers were also reportedly considering measures to prevent strategically important domestic technologies from being transferred abroad, acquired by foreign companies, or produced overseas. If these strict proposals were approved by the CCP and the government, Chinese chip designers would be unable to produce their chips at TSMC in Taiwan or Samsung Foundry in South Korea, and would force them to exclusively make them domestically at Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp., Hua Hong, and other domestic contract producers that are decades behind market leaders.The report claims the updated regulations reflect the strategic importance China now assigns to technologies developed by its domestic semiconductor industry. For now, it is evident that China is not ready to implement overseas production of advanced designs. However, the report does not explicitly claim they are completely off the table, according to Reuters. history.titleZh: 中国严厉打击山寨芯片设计，新规与处罚并举——新指南强制要求原创与自主研发
history.descriptionZh:
中国国务院修订了集成电路（IC）布图设计保护相关法规，旨在加强国内芯片设计的原创性要求、登记程序和侵权救济，使那些依赖抄袭竞争对手芯片设计的中国企业更难获得法律保护。新规由国务院总理李强于7月23日签署，将于10月15日正式生效。此次修订反映出中国政府对本土半导体产业技术成果战略价值的重视，同时也在平衡产业保护与国际生产布局之间的关系。

新规主要针对物理芯片布图设计——即定义硅片上电路元件排列方式、体现大量工程工作的设计，同样适用于专注于芯片设计而非制造的公司。为了获得IC布图设计的法律保护，申请方现在必须证明该布图是独立开发的，正式声明设计具有原创性，并明确指出哪些部分属于自身的创造性贡献，以便当局了解哪些部分可能是授权或开源的。这一要求使得监管部门能够筛选出实力较弱的申请，区分真正具备技术能力的公司与那些从外部获取产品并试图伪装成“中国制造”芯片的开发者。此外，新规还强化了执法力度：自10月中旬起，在侵权纠纷中，法院可以基于权利人遭受的损失或侵权方获得的利润来确定赔偿金额，并可适用惩罚性赔偿。新规还澄清了布图设计权的许可、转让和质押程序，同时要求拥有受保护布图设计的机构对参与开发的人员提供合理的奖励和报酬。

值得注意的是，该报道提到中国政策制定者曾考虑采取措施防止战略性国内技术被转移至海外、被外国公司收购或在境外生产。如果这些严格提案获得批准，中国芯片设计公司将无法在台积电（TSMC）的台湾工厂或三星晶圆代工厂（Samsung Foundry）生产芯片，而只能完全依赖中芯国际（SMIC）、华虹等国内代工厂——这些厂商与全球领先水平仍有数十年差距。最终公布的新规并未包含此类境外生产禁令，表明中国政府目前尚未准备对先进设计实施全面的海外生产限制，但也没有完全排除这种可能性。

这一修订发生在全球半导体格局深刻变化的背景下：美国在芯片出口管制政策上反复摇摆，中国大陆则持续构建自主芯片供应链，台湾地区也在酝酿对华AI芯片出口的刑事禁令，甚至出现台积电前高管因涉嫌为中国窃取芯片机密而被起诉的案件。新规的实施将有助于中国在鼓励本土芯片设计创新的同时，防范技术抄袭和资产流失，对国内芯片产业的健康发展具有重要的法律和战略意义。
